chapters.category: Ethiopic textual tradition • Modern English research translation
chapters.title: Chapter 63 — The Rulers’ Late Confession
chapters.sourceNote: Translated afresh into clear modern English from the earliest complete primary-language text responsibly available for this chapter. No extant Aramaic or Greek wording has been identified for the Parables. The complete Ethiopic (Geʽez) text in August Dillmann's 1851 critical edition, Liber Henoch Aethiopice, is the translation base for all twelve verses: the condemned rulers' request for respite, their confession of the Lord's hidden wisdom and righteous judgment, their admission that wealth and royal glory became their hope, and their final expulsion before the Son of Man. The confession's first-person plural voice and the sequence from requested rest to irreversible darkness are retained. No unattested wording was supplied, and no modern English translation was used as the translation base.

verses.text: In those days the kings and mighty ones who possess the dry ground will petition the angels of punishment to whom they have been handed over, asking them to grant a little rest so that they may fall down and worship before the Lord of Spirits and confess their sins before Him.
verses.study: The rulers finally desire worship and confession, but only after being handed to punishment. Their request for a little rest exposes how long they delayed recognition.
crossReferences: Luke 16:23–31 — a condemned rich man asks relief after opportunity has passed
Revelation 6:15–17 — rulers seek escape when the day of wrath arrives

verses.text: They will bless and glorify the Lord of Spirits and say, ‘Blessed is the Lord of Spirits, the Lord of kings, the Lord of the mighty, the Lord of the rich, the Lord of glory and the Lord of wisdom, who brings every hidden thing to light.’
verses.study: Their titles confess that every status they claimed belonged above all to God. Hidden deeds and motives now stand in His light.
crossReferences: Daniel 2:20–22 — wisdom, power and hidden things belong to God
1 Timothy 6:15–16 — God is King of kings and Lord of lords

verses.text: ‘Your power endures from generation to generation, and Your glory forever and ever. All Your hidden things are deep and beyond number, and Your righteousness is beyond calculation.’
verses.study: The confession contrasts God's immeasurable righteousness with the rulers' temporary power. His secrets exceed counting, while their deeds have been fully counted.
crossReferences: Psalm 145:3–5 — God's greatness and glorious works span generations
Romans 11:33 — God's judgments and ways are unsearchably deep

verses.text: ‘Now we know that we should glorify and bless the Lord of kings, the One who reigns over all kings.’
verses.study: Knowledge arrives at last, but confession after judgment is not the same as faithful recognition during the time of mercy.
crossReferences: Psalm 47:7–9 — God reigns over the nations and their rulers
Philippians 2:10–11 — every knee bows and every tongue confesses the Lord

verses.text: They will say, ‘Who will grant us rest so that we may glorify, thank and bless Him and confess before His glory?’
verses.study: The request joins relief to worship, yet they no longer control their time. The opportunity they treated as expendable has become the mercy they cannot command.
crossReferences: Isaiah 55:6 — the LORD must be sought while He may be found
Hebrews 3:12–15 — response is required while it is called today

verses.text: ‘Even now we long for a little rest, but we do not find it. We are driven away and cannot take hold of it. Light has passed away from before us, and darkness is our dwelling forever and ever.’
verses.study: Their condition reverses Chapter 58: the chosen receive unending light, but rulers who rejected it cannot grasp even brief rest and inherit darkness.
crossReferences: Matthew 8:11–12 — those expecting privilege may be cast into outer darkness
John 12:35–36 — light must be trusted while it is present

verses.text: ‘For we did not believe before Him, nor did we glorify the name of the Lord of kings or glorify the Lord in all His works. Our hope was in the scepter of our kingdom and in our own glory.’
verses.study: The rulers name their central error: misplaced trust. Political authority and public glory became substitutes for faith and praise.
crossReferences: Psalm 49:6–13 — trust in wealth and honor cannot prevent death
Daniel 4:28–32 — royal self-glory is humbled before heaven's rule

verses.text: ‘On the day of our suffering and distress He does not save us, and we find no rest. We confess that our Lord is faithful in all His deeds, in all His judgments and in His righteousness, and that His judgment shows no partiality.’
verses.study: Their confession vindicates the Judge even while it cannot undo the verdict. God's faithfulness includes impartial judgment of privileged rulers.
crossReferences: Deuteronomy 10:17 — God shows no partiality and accepts no bribe
Romans 2:5–11 — righteous judgment repays deeds without favoritism

verses.text: ‘We pass away from before His face because of our deeds, and all our sins have been counted in righteousness.’
verses.study: The final accounting is exact and moral. They are not removed arbitrarily; their own deeds and counted sins explain the sentence.
crossReferences: Psalm 90:8 — hidden sins are set in the light of God's presence
Revelation 20:12 — the dead are judged according to recorded deeds

verses.text: Now they will say, ‘Our souls are satisfied with the wealth of injustice, but it does not prevent our descent into the flame of the torment of Sheol.’
verses.study: Unjust wealth satisfied desire without providing rescue. What once seemed sufficient proves powerless at the descent it cannot stop.
crossReferences: Proverbs 11:4 — riches do not profit in the day of wrath
James 5:1–5 — hoarded wealth testifies against oppressive luxury

verses.text: After this their faces will be filled with darkness and shame before that Son of Man. They will be driven from before his face, and a sword will remain before him among them.
verses.study: The confession closes in the same shame and expulsion announced in Chapter 62. The Son of Man's presence exposes rather than conceals their history.
crossReferences: Daniel 12:2 — resurrection can lead to shame and lasting contempt
Revelation 19:15 — the enthroned ruler judges with a sharp sword

verses.text: Thus says the Lord of Spirits: ‘This is the portion and judgment of the mighty, the kings, the exalted, and those who possess the dry ground before the Lord of Spirits.’
verses.study: The Lord Himself identifies the outcome as their allotted judgment. Earthly possession cannot alter the portion assigned before the true Lord.
crossReferences: Psalm 75:7–8 — God brings rulers down and assigns the cup of judgment
Revelation 19:17–21 — kings and mighty ones meet the judgment of the heavenly ruler

explanation.heading: Chapter teaching and context
paragraphs: Chapter 63 gives condemned rulers their own voice. They confess the Lord's supremacy, wisdom, hidden knowledge and impartial righteousness, but their recognition comes only after the time for faithful response has passed.
Their repeated request for a little rest answers their former possession of the earth. Those who controlled the lives of others cannot now command even a moment of relief.
The rulers identify the spiritual center of their failure: they trusted the scepter of their kingdom, their glory and wealth gained through injustice. Those supports satisfy desire but cannot save.

Their confession vindicates divine judgment without overturning it. Counted sins, darkness, shame and expulsion become the measured portion of powers that refused to glorify the Lord during the day of mercy.

crossReferences: Daniel 4:28–32 — royal pride humbled before heavenly sovereignty
Psalm 49:6–13 — wealth and honor unable to redeem life
Romans 2:5–11 — impartial judgment according to deeds
Philippians 2:10–11 — universal confession of lordship
Revelation 20:12 — deeds opened for judgment
